title: Backend (live-animals): malformed request bodies return 500 instead of 400 — GlobalExceptionHandler's RuntimeException catch-all swallows framework exceptions
recipe: No recipe. pp-068 fixed the identical defect in the plant-products package — read PlantProductsExceptionHandler and its commit e2fbdaf first and transpose that shape, so the two handlers stay aligned.

filesToTouch.what: A malformed JSON body returns 500 instead of 400. Proved against the real HTTP stack during pp-068: a malformed POST /notifications returns 500. ROOT CAUSE, established in pp-068 and expected to be the same here: the handler carries a RuntimeException catch-all that intercepts Spring's own HttpMessageNotReadableException — which the framework would otherwise resolve to 400 — and maps it to 500. Handle unreadable bodies explicitly, ahead of the catch-all, returning the house problem-style 400 with no stack-trace content. THE CATCH-ALL ITSELF IS THE REAL QUESTION: HttpMessageNotReadableException is not special, it is merely the instance we caught. Any Spring framework exception that extends RuntimeException — unsupported media type, method not allowed, missing parameter, type mismatch — is liable to the same downgrade to 500. Enumerate which ones the catch-all currently swallows and fix the class of problem, not only the one instance.

Prove the corrected behaviour over the real HTTP stack for every endpoint family that accepts a body — notifications, fulfilment and the document sub-resource: a malformed body, a literal-null body and a missing body each return 400 with the problem-style shape. Assert at the integration layer, NOT only in a @WebMvcTest slice — the whole reason this defect survived is that a slice proved the opposite.

Audit the animals @WebMvcTest slices for the same incomplete-context defect pp-068 found in plant-products: a slice that omits GlobalExceptionHandler exercises Spring's default exception resolution rather than production's, so its status-code assertions can be green while production is broken. Report how many assertions run on the incomplete stack and make the slices representative. Do not delete assertions to resolve a contradiction — a slice and an IT disagreeing means production is wrong, or the slice is.

specs: IT: a malformed JSON body returns 400 with the problem-style shape and no stack-trace content, on every animals endpoint family that accepts a body.
IT: a literal-null body and a missing body each return 400 rather than 500.
Any other Spring framework RuntimeException the catch-all was downgrading now maps to its correct status.
acceptanceCriteria: A malformed request body returns 400, not 500, proved by integration tests over the real HTTP stack for every animals endpoint family that accepts a body.

The GlobalExceptionHandler RuntimeException catch-all no longer downgrades framework exceptions that have a correct status of their own. The set of exceptions it was swallowing is enumerated in the commit message.

The animals @WebMvcTest slices load the same exception-handling stack as production, so a slice can no longer be green where the application is broken. The number of assertions previously running on the incomplete stack is reported.
No existing behaviour changes for well-formed requests: every pre-existing animals unit test and IT still passes without its assertions being edited.
mvn verify is green end to end.
notes:
RAISED DURING THE BUILD (orchestrator, 2026-08-01) — a defect in ALREADY-SHIPPED live-animals code, found by transposition for the second time tonight. pp-068 fixed the identical bug in the plant-products package and, while proving the root cause, probed the animals endpoints and found a malformed POST /notifications returns 500 there too. The pp-068 increment's own text asserted that animals already handled this case correctly; that assertion was wrong, which is worth remembering when a plan claims the incumbent implementation is sound.

WHY IT CARRIES A GATE: it changes exception handling on shipped API surface, and the fix's blast radius is deliberately wider than one endpoint — narrowing a catch-all changes the status code of anything it was previously absorbing. That is exactly the change a human should look at before it lands.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE 400: the catch-all is the defect. HttpMessageNotReadableException is just the instance that surfaced, and any framework RuntimeException with a meaningful status of its own is liable to the same downgrade. A client currently cannot distinguish 'your request was malformed' from 'the server broke', on shipped API surface.

SEE ALSO pp-069, the other shipped-animals defect found the same way. Both were invisible until a second implementation was built beside the first and reviewed harder than the original ever was.
openQuestions: Does the animals handler downgrade other framework exceptions too — unsupported media type, method not allowed, missing request parameter, argument type mismatch? The implementor should enumerate before fixing; if several are affected the increment is larger than 'malformed body' and the title should be corrected.

Do pp-069 and this increment share a root cause worth addressing once — i.e. is there a house pattern for exception handling and transactional boundaries that both packages copied? Worth a look before fixing them independently.
Should these two shipped-code defects be raised as Jira tickets rather than carried in this programme's backlog? The orchestrator's view is yes for both; no ticket has been raised.
